correctness.rationale: Explicit tetrahedron opposition-edge enumeration proves a graph decomposition. The categorical product connectedness uses gcd(2,m,n)=1. Two three-step detours show that deletion of the two marked categorical-product edges leaves it connected; the complete bipartite piece remains connected after deleting one. The four connected pieces glue along six facet ports, and the marked perfect matching is preserved for exactly eight permutations. Exact Euler graph ranks give both integral wedge decompositions; direct facet-based checks reproduce 16 parameter pairs and all 24 bijections in the finite example. No finite extrapolation is used.
